Server-side DNS and network reachability are working. The remaining issue is macOS resolution path/cache.

First fix the resolver file permissions so `sc dns status` can see it:

```bash
sudo chmod 755 /etc/resolver
sudo chmod 644 /etc/resolver/sandman
sc dns status
```

Then flush macOS DNS:

```bash
sudo dscacheutil -flushcache
sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
```

Test with macOS’s resolver stack, not `dig @...`:

```bash
dscacheutil -q host -a name pages.sandboxes.sandman
ping pages.sandboxes.sandman
```

If that still fails, remove the search-domain collision. Your `scutil --dns` shows your normal Wi-Fi DNS also has `search domain[1] : sandman` pointing at `10.10.2.254`, while `/etc/resolver/sandman` points at `10.206.10.5`. The domain-scoped resolver should win, but the search domain can make debugging noisy.

Run:

```bash
sc dns search remove
sc dns install
sudo dscacheutil -flushcache
sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
ping pages.sandboxes.sandman
```

If you want short names later, add the project-specific search domain instead:

```bash
sc dns search add --project sandboxes
```

But first get the full FQDN working.
